Items.Title: Pin Phaser dependency and lockfile with standalone version validation
Items.Description: Select the exact Phaser package within the approved engine direction, commit the dependency and lockfile to the authorized branch, and add restore/version assertions without creating a duplicate prerequisite.
AcceptanceCriteria: One coherent engineering deliverable selects the exact Phaser package version within the approved Phaser direction, commits it with a reproducible lockfile to the assignment's authorized branch, and restores dependencies without adding a second prerequisite ticket for the same outcome.
A standalone assertion command such as npm test or node scripts/verify-pin.mjs fails if the installed Phaser version differs from the committed pin or if the lockfile is absent or inconsistent.

Items.Title: Boot placeholder Phaser scene in Chromium latest stable
Items.Description: Start the committed project as a desktop-web placeholder Phaser scene in Chromium latest stable without blocking runtime or console errors.
AcceptanceCriteria: The committed project starts as a desktop-web build in Chromium latest stable from the platform-assigned immutable candidate and the actual Story target branch, showing a browser-visible placeholder Phaser scene without blocking runtime or console errors.

Items.Title: Commit local best-score persistence spike with automated reload test
Items.Description: Select and commit a local browser storage mechanism for best-score persistence, and add an automated Chromium write/clear/read reload test under normal browser storage behaviour.
AcceptanceCriteria: The increment selects and commits a local browser storage mechanism for best-score persistence, with an automated test that writes, clears, and reads a key across page reload in Chromium under normal browser storage behaviour.

Items.Title: Implement minimal core scene and assemble first-increment candidate evidence
Items.Description: Add minimal paddle/ball/brick interactions, an internal score counter, and placeholder readability checks; assemble candidate-scoped command, pin, run, and persistence evidence without claiming approval or release.
AcceptanceCriteria: The minimal scene demonstrates mouse paddle X movement, click-to-launch, arrow-key paddle movement, and one ball interaction that destroys a brick and updates an internal score counter.
The placeholder primary ball silhouette remains legible during launch, paddle bounce, wall bounce, and brick destruction with no presentation FX.

Evidence from the assigned candidate includes command output, committed pin/lockfile, a short observed run record, and a persistence test result; no Director acceptance, QA sign-off, integration into main, or release is claimed.

60 fps remains a normal-play target, not a hard measured gate; no profiling or stress testing is performed unless observed instability or readability loss occurs, in which case it is raised for technical review.
